title: land runs selfdoc stale over the range before the stress run
goal: backlog.py land runs selfdoc.py stale --since <integration main> over the rebased range right after the rebase, before stress_test.py, the lookup eval and the lint, and stops at a step named stale, so a missing Self-Reviewed trailer fails in seconds; a stacked item whose lower item has landed loses that item's Self-Reviewed coverage and is caught the same way. Answers SP-5cwekumc's retrospective: six lands reached sync's stale gate only after a five-minute stress run (ST-g3w7v3el, ST-vfct2532 and four stacked branches).
notes: Merged finding: the cause of the late stale failure in two sessions is a worker brief that puts the Self-Reviewed trailer in a paragraph of its own before KB-Work; git reads trailers from the last paragraph only, so the gate saw no Self-Reviewed (a rerun of a full land, about 25 minutes, and about two retries over a doc another session edited). The worker brief states that Self-Reviewed goes inside the last trailer paragraph with KB-Work, and a test fails when the kb-worker definition or the kb-sprint brief text lacks it. Merged finding, second brief clause: kb-worker workers stalled more than once with changes staged, no commit and their test run gone, because they waited for a background-run completion notice that never arrived (ST-pvu4ecpv; the orchestrator finished it by hand, hours lost on a chain that holds the fleet's shared files). The worker brief says to run the item's checks and tests in the foreground with a timeout and never to wait for a background completion notice; a test fails when the kb-worker definition lacks it.
